claim.quote: Here we report the development of an antihydrogen source using a cusp trap for in-flight spectroscopy.

key_value_text.quote: A total of 80 antihydrogen atoms are unambiguously detected 2.7 m downstream of the production region
key_value_text.value: 80 antihydrogen atoms detected 2.7 m downstream of the production region

name: A source of antihydrogen for in-flight hyperfine spectroscopy

significance.quote: A total of 80 antihydrogen atoms are unambiguously detected 2.7 m downstream of the production region
significance.value: 80 antihydrogen atoms unambiguously detected downstream (no sigma level stated in the abstract)

summary.plain: ASACUSA built an antihydrogen source using a cusp magnet and detected 80 antihydrogen atoms 2.7 metres downstream of where they were made, where stray magnetic fields are small. This is a step towards measuring their hyperfine structure.
summary.technical: Cusp-trap antihydrogen source for in-flight spectroscopy: a total of 80 antihydrogen atoms unambiguously detected 2.7 m downstream of the production region, a step towards Rabi-like beam spectroscopy of the ground-state hyperfine splitting.

title: A source of antihydrogen for in-flight hyperfine spectroscopy
why_it_matters: The abstract says high-resolution comparisons of hydrogen and antihydrogen sensitively test CPT symmetry and any difference would point to new physics.
